concerns.text: Task T012 (tokenizer.py) is marked [P] and depends on T009, but it also implicitly depends on T002 (requirements.txt) to install the 'transformers' library required for the frozen VLM. Without T002 completed, T012 cannot execute. The [P] tag is invalid as it ignores this hard dependency.

Tasks T013, T014, and T015 (graph_builder.py) are marked [P] and depend on T009. However, they also depend on T012 (tokenizer.py) to produce the semantic tokens required to construct the DAG nodes. The current order implies T013 can run in parallel with T012, which is impossible as T013 consumes T012's output.

Tasks T020-T022 (query_engine.py) are marked [P] and depend on Foundational phase. However, they logically depend on the output of User Story 1 (T013-T015) which constructs the symbolic graph. The query engine cannot execute on a graph that hasn't been built. The [P] tag and parallel execution assumption are invalid.

Task T028 (experiment_runner.py) is listed in Phase 5 (US3) but depends on T016 (sweep execution in US1) and T027 (baseline runner). The current ordering places T016 as uncompleted (unchecked) and T028 as a primary task, creating a consumer-before-producer violation for the sweep metrics and baseline data.

Task T031 depends on T016. T016 is currently unchecked (not completed). T031 cannot be executed or even started until T016 produces the 'sweep_metrics.csv'. The dependency chain is broken in the current task list state.

Task T032 depends on T032a. T032a is unchecked. T032 cannot proceed. Furthermore, T032 depends on the completion of the comparative study (T028) and statistical tests (T029), which are not explicitly listed as prerequisites in the 'Depends on' clause of T032, creating a hidden ordering risk.

The 'Parallel Opportunities' section claims 'All user stories can start in parallel'. This is semantically incorrect. US2 (Query Engine) and US3 (Comparative Analysis) cannot start until US1 (Graph Construction) produces the symbolic graph artifact. The text contradicts the actual data-flow dependencies.
